questions.question: Explain main replication cycle in Bacteriophage.
questions.solution_html:

questions.solution_html:
• Compare the similarities of Prokaryotic and Eukaryotic cell.
  • Both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells share fundamental similarities, including the presence of a cell
  • membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes, and DNA as their genetic material. Both types also perform basic life
  • processes such as metabolism and reproduction.

questions.question: Define golden age of Microbiology.
questions.solution_html:
• The "golden age of Microbiology" refers to the period from the mid-1800s to the early 1900s, during which
  • numerous fundamental discoveries were made. Key figures like Louis Pasteur and Robert Koch established
  • microbiology as a science, identifying many pathogens and developing techniques like pasteurization and
  • germ theory.

questions.question: Illustrate the ultrastructure of bacteria and their functions. /.(Diagram -1 Mark
questions.solution_html:
• Explanation -(2 Marks), Function -(1 Mark))
  • Bacteria have a simple prokaryotic ultrastructure including a cell wall, membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes
  • and a nucleoid. Key features are the absence of membrane-bound organelles and a true nucleus. Functions
  • include protection (cell wall), selective transport (membrane), protein synthesis (ribosomes), and genetic
  • information storage (nucleoid).

questions.question: Differentiate the Economic important of Ascomycota and Basidiomycota. /. (Economic
questions.solution_html:
• Importance of Ascomycota -(2 Marks), Economic important of Basidiomycota -(2 Marks))
  • Ascomycota and Basidiomycota have distinct economic roles, primarily in food production and
  • decomposition .Ascomycota includes beneficial organisms like Saccharomyces (brewing/baking) and
  • edible truffles, but also plant pathogens like Dutch elm disease. Basidiomycota are mainly known for edible
  • mushrooms (like button mushrooms) and are significant decomposers of wood, playing a vital role in
  • nutrient cycling, though some are also plant pathogens.
questions.final_answer: nutrient cycling, though some are also plant pathogens

questions.question: Discuss the morphological feature of Bacterial cell wall. / (Differentiate Gram positive
questions.solution_html:
• and Gram Negative bacterial cell wall -(2 Mark) each)
  • Bacterial cell walls are primarily composed of peptidoglycan and provide shape and structural integrity.The
  • cell wall is a rigid layer outside the plasma membrane. Gram-positive bacteria have a thick peptidoglycan
  • layer, while Gram-negative bacteria have a thin peptidoglycan layer and an outer membrane containing
  • lipopolysaccharides. This structure protects the cell from osmotic lysis and determines the bacterial cell's
  • shape.

questions.question: Explain the detailed note on Bacteriophage. /. (Define Bacteriophage -1 mark , Life Cycle
questions.solution_html:
• – (2 Marks), Diagram -(2 Marks))
  • A bacteriophage is a virus that specifically infects bacteria .Bacteriophages, or phages, are composed of
  • a protein coat enclosing genetic material (DNA or RNA). They replicate by inserting their genome into the
  • host bacterium, either through a lytic cycle (killing the host cell) or a lysogenic cycle (integrating into the
  • host genome). They are widely studied in molecular biology and have potential applications in phage
  • therapy.

  • Aspergillus - (2 Marks) , Characteristics of Penicillium – (2 Marks))

  • importance. Aspergillus species are known for producing toxins (like aflatoxin) and causing diseases, but
  • some are used in fermentation. Penicillium is famous as the source of the antibiotic penicillin and is used
  • in cheese making. Morphologically, Aspergillus typically has a single row of phialides on a vesicle, while
  • Penicillium has a brush-like (penicillus) arrangement of conidiophore.
questions.final_answer: Penicillium has a brush-like (penicillus) arrangement of conidiophore

questions.question: Illustrate the ultrastructure of bacteria and their functions. /.(Diagram -1 Mark
questions.solution_html:
• Explanation -(2 Marks), Function -(1 Mark))
  • Bacteria have a simple prokaryotic ultrastructure including a cell wall, membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes
  • and a nucleoid. Key features are the absence of membrane-bound organelles and a true nucleus. Functions
  • include protection (cell wall), selective transport (membrane), protein synthesis (ribosomes), and genetic
  • information storage (nucleoid).

questions.question: Differentiate the Economic important of Ascomycota and Basidiomycota. /. (Economic
questions.solution_html:
• Importance of Ascomycota -(2 Marks), Economic important of Basidiomycota -(2 Marks))
  • Ascomycota and Basidiomycota have distinct economic roles, primarily in food production and
  • decomposition .Ascomycota includes beneficial organisms like Saccharomyces (brewing/baking) and
  • edible truffles, but also plant pathogens like Dutch elm disease. Basidiomycota are mainly known for edible

  • nutrient cycling, though some are also plant pathogens.

questions.question: Discuss the morphological feature of Bacterial cell wall. / (Differentiate Gram positive
questions.solution_html:
• and Gram Negative bacterial cell wall -(2 Mark) each)
  • Bacterial cell walls are primarily composed of peptidoglycan and provide shape and structural integrity.The
  • cell wall is a rigid layer outside the plasma membrane. Gram-positive bacteria have a thick peptidoglycan
  • layer, while Gram-negative bacteria have a thin peptidoglycan layer and an outer membrane containing
  • lipopolysaccharides. This structure protects the cell from osmotic lysis and determines the bacterial cell's
  • shape.

questions.question: Explain the detailed note on Bacteriophage. /. (Define Bacteriophage -1 mark , Life Cycle
questions.solution_html:
• – (2 Marks), Diagram -(2 Marks))
  • A bacteriophage is a virus that specifically infects bacteria .Bacteriophages, or phages, are composed of
  • a protein coat enclosing genetic material (DNA or RNA). They replicate by inserting their genome into the
  • host bacterium, either through a lytic cycle (killing the host cell) or a lysogenic cycle (integrating into the
  • host genome). They are widely studied in molecular biology and have potential applications in phage
  • therapy.

questions.question: Question 29
questions.solution_html:
• Compare the characteristic feature of Aspergillus and Penicillium. /.(Characteristics of
  • Aspergillus - (2 Marks) , Characteristics of Penicillium – (2 Marks))
  • Aspergillus and Penicillium are both filamentous fungi with distinct conidial structures and economic
  • importance. Aspergillus species are known for producing toxins (like aflatoxin) and causing diseases, but
  • some are used in fermentation. Penicillium is famous as the source of the antibiotic penicillin and is used
  • in cheese making. Morphologically, Aspergillus typically has a single row of phialides on a vesicle, while
  • Penicillium has a brush-like (penicillus) arrangement of conidiophore.
questions.final_answer: Penicillium has a brush-like (penicillus) arrangement of conidiophore
